# Sync architecture

Muninn sync is manual, one provider per vault, and one active writer per vault.
The note files remain the source of truth. The sync journal, checkpoints, and
last converged snapshot live under the XDG state directory, outside the vault.
They are bookkeeping, not a second copy of the user's notes as the canonical store.

## What success means

A successful run means the included files match one published snapshot and the
local journal for that run is complete. It does not mean a single filesystem
transaction, real-time collaborative editing, or that a program outside Muninn
was frozen for the whole time.

The first bind has no deletion authority: files that exist on only one side are
copied, and a same-path disagreement is a conflict. Later deletes are explicit
tombstones. A missing page, a 403, or a 404 is not a delete.

A conflict between this device and the remote (the same note edited on both
since the last sync, an edit against a delete, a rename against an edit, or the
same new path on both) does not stop sync. The app resolves every conflict as
"keep both" on every provider: this device's version keeps the path, and the
remote version, if there is one, is written beside it as `<stem> (remote)<ext>`
(`(remote 2)` and so on if that name is taken). The status line names each copy.
Changes outside the conflicting paths in the same run (one-sided edits,
deletes, renames) apply as usual. A path that still exists with new bytes is
never read as the source of a rename, so a copy holding the old bytes is an add,
not a move. A rename on one side onto a name the other side now uses for
different bytes is not applied as a rename: it becomes a delete of the old name
and a same-name add on both sides, kept as `<name>` (this device) and
`<name> (remote)` (the other), so neither note is overwritten. The same holds when both sides renamed one note to different names and either name is taken by different bytes on the other side: both renames are declined. Per-file Keep local / Use remote choices are not in the app yet.

## Credentials

Tokens live in the OS credential store (`keyring` v1: macOS Keychain, Windows
Credential Manager, Linux Secret Service). If that store is missing, locked, or
refuses the request, sync stops. There is no plaintext file fallback. Settings
store the public client id, the binding id, and the remote scope only.

Access tokens carry an absolute expiry. A run refreshes a token within five
minutes of expiry, and refreshes once after a 401; the new pair is stored
before it is used. Sign-in runs on a worker thread: GitHub device flow, or
Google OAuth with PKCE and a `127.0.0.1` loopback redirect, both in the system
browser (fixed program, URL as one argument, `https` only).

Disconnect deletes that binding's credential and the settings entry. It does
not delete local notes, remote notes, or checkpoints.

# Privacy Policy

Effective date: November 9, 2026

Muninn is a local-first notes app made by Raymond Thurman, doing business as Ravenwood Software. This policy describes what happens when you use optional sync.

### Google Drive

If you connect Google Drive, Muninn asks only for access to this app's hidden app folder in Drive (`drive.appdata`). Muninn cannot see, read, or change the rest of your Drive files. The sync store is not visible in the Drive website. It counts against your Google storage. If you revoke Muninn's access in your Google Account, Google deletes that hidden store; the notes on your devices are not deleted.

## What we do not collect

Muninn does not create a Muninn account, and the app does not send your notes or usage data to us. Google, GitHub, and Tailscale may keep their own records of sign-in and API use under their policies.

## Google Drive

The bundled client is a Desktop app client in project Muninn
(`muninn-514218`), consent app "Muninn", scope `drive.appdata` only, PKCE plus
the build-time client secret above. To use your own Google project instead:

1. Create a Google Cloud project.
2. Enable the Google Drive API. No Picker API is needed.
3. Configure the OAuth consent screen, with a privacy policy URL, and publish
   it to production. `drive.appdata` is a non-sensitive scope.
4. Create a Desktop OAuth client. Build Muninn with its id in
   `MUNINN_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` and its secret in `MUNINN_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`.
   Never commit or paste the secret. A custom id typed into Settings → Sync →
   Drive → Google client id fails closed, because Muninn has no secret for it.
5. Muninn requests only `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.appdata`, with
   PKCE S256, a random `state`, and a loopback redirect on
   `http://127.0.0.1:<random port>/callback`. It does not request full Drive,
   `drive.file`, email, or profile scopes.
6. Connect opens Google's consent page (`accounts.google.com`) in the system
   browser. After consent, Google redirects to the loopback listener, Muninn
   exchanges the code at `oauth2.googleapis.com`, and the tokens go to the OS
   credential store. The wait times out after five minutes; Disconnect cancels
   it.
7. Drive sync keeps its data in the app's hidden `appDataFolder`, in a root
   folder named `muninn-sync-<store name>` with `blobs` and `commits` inside.
   Use the same store name on every device that shares the vault, and a
   different one for another vault on the same Google account.

### Why `appDataFolder`

`drive.file` only reaches files this app created or that the person opened
with it (for example with the Google Picker), so a pasted folder id never
worked without a Picker. `drive.appdata` reaches only the app's own hidden
folder: no Picker, a non-sensitive scope, and every device signed in with the
same account and OAuth client sees the same store. The costs: the store is not
visible or editable in the Drive UI, it counts against the account's storage,
and revoking Muninn's access in the Google Account deletes it (the notes on
each device are not affected). Those objects are not Markdown files either
way; do not expect to edit notes in Drive.

## Linux credentials

The credential store is Secret Service over the session D-Bus. The collection
has to be unlocked. If it is missing or locked, sync reports that credentials
are unavailable. It does not write the token to a file.

macOS uses Keychain Services. Windows uses Credential Manager. Those prompts
and signing requirements were not exercised in this environment.

## What it does

- **Write / Read / Graph** modes for the same note.
- Autosave after a short idle, with a `Saved` indicator in the status bar.
- Searchable note list grouped by folder with collapsing sections, a links rail with outgoing links
  and backlinks (including the line that made each link), and a one-click local graph.
- **Global** and **Local** graph views. Local keeps the open note and its immediate neighbours.
  Selecting a node glides the camera to it, and switching scopes eases the camera into the
  new framing while the nodes that enter or leave fade.
- Dragging a graph node pins it while you drag; the force layout settles around it. Drag the
  background to pan, scroll to zoom at the pointer, Shift+scroll to pan, pinch or Ctrl/Cmd+scroll
  to zoom.
- The graph is keyboard-complete: arrows move a focus ring between visible notes, `Enter` opens
  the focused note, `+`/`-` zoom, `0`/`F` fit, and `Esc` leaves. The **Find node** field selects
  and centres a title or path; **Isolate** dims everything outside the selection's neighbourhood.
  Hub notes draw larger, and at far zoom labels thin to dots in Local as well as Global.
- Unresolved wikilinks are drawn faintly in Read mode. Clicking one creates the note and opens
  it in Write mode. Path-qualified links (`[[folder/note]]`) resolve to that folder; a bare
  title shared by several notes resolves deterministically and displays with its folder.
- Attachments are files, not notes: only `.md` files are indexed. An embed such as
  `![[pic.png]]` renders in Read mode as a filename-and-size placeholder, not a faint missing
  note link, and the reader's attachment strip lists each file with **Open**. Rune's Markdown
  view has no image pipeline in this revision and `Tx::open_url` refuses `file:` URLs, so Open
  hands the canonical path to the platform handler instead (`xdg-open` on Linux, `open` on
  macOS, `start` on Windows). Right-click a note for **Open externally** and **Reveal in file
  manager**.
- Drop files on the window to import them into the current folder: `.md` becomes a note and
  opens, while png/jpg/jpeg/gif/webp/pdf files are copied as attachments that stay out of the
  sidebar (the status bar reports the count). Imports are atomic copies and never overwrite:
  an existing filename is refused with its name. File drops work on macOS, Windows and X11;
  Wayland reports no file drags to winit 0.30, so dropping from a file manager there does
  nothing — use the sidebar actions instead.
- Word count uses whitespace splitting, so a CJK run without spaces counts as one word
  (documented, not locale-aware segmentation). Unicode titles (CJK, accents, RTL) search and
  resolve by the same case-folded title/path rules as ASCII.
- **New note** asks for a name first (empty or cancelled creates nothing) and targets the
  current or chosen folder. Right-click a note or folder for rename, delete, move and
  new-note/new-folder actions; rename/delete also appear with `F2` and `Delete`. …

## Crate graph

```text
muninn-app ──► muninn-ui ──► muninn-graph ──► muninn-core
     │              │
     │              └──► muninn-sync
     └──────────────┴──► rune, rune-kit, rune-theme-opencode
```

| Crate | May depend on | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `muninn-core` | nothing in the workspace | Pure domain model; fast unit tests. |
| `muninn-graph` | `muninn-core` | Needs note ids and links, nothing else. |
| `muninn-sync` | nothing in the workspace | Plans and transfers vault bytes. It does not read the UI or the link index. |
| `muninn-ui` | `muninn-core`, `muninn-graph`, `muninn-sync`, Rune | Owns state, rendering, input, and the manual sync session. |
| `muninn-app` | `muninn-ui`, Rune | Entry point only. It may also depend on `muninn-sync` for credential wiring. |
| `xtask` | tooling crates | Never linked into the app. |

`cargo run -p xtask -- layers` reads `cargo metadata` and rejects any new `muninn-*` edge that
is not in this table. That check is part of `xtask check` and CI.

The `muninn` binary's headless `--check` and `--list-links` paths read `muninn-core` directly
(and `--check` never creates a missing vault) before Rune starts a window or GPU context.

## Parsing rules

`[[target]]`, `[[target|alias]]` and `[[target#heading]]` are supported. A target resolves
case-insensitively by:

1. **Path-qualified** (`[[folder/note]]`): exact vault-relative stem, then a unique
   `/`-suffixed tail. No match means missing — never a bare-title fallback.
2. **Unambiguous title** (`[[Title]]`): exactly one note has that title.
3. **Duplicate titles**: the deterministic smallest vault-relative path (case-insensitive,
   then case-sensitive). The preview always renders a note's full stem, so rendered links
   do not depend on this fallback.

Links to the current note are allowed in the source but do not produce self-edges in the graph.
Unresolved targets stay in the source, render faintly, and create a note when clicked —
path-qualified ones inside their folder, bare ones in the current note's folder.
New notes otherwise target the selected note's folder; each folder header's `+` chooses a
different one. Dot-directories stay ignored by the scan. Heading links
(`[[Note#Heading]]`) resolve the note and then put the Write caret on that heading line or
scroll the Read view to it, matching case-insensitively outside fenced blocks; a missing
heading opens the note at the top. Rename/move rewrites only targets that resolved to the
note before the change, so a bare duplicate title that resolved elsewhere is untouched.

## Scaling notes

- New non-UI behaviour belongs in `muninn-core` or `muninn-graph` with unit tests.
- New screens belong in `muninn-ui`; keep `muninn-app` to wiring.
- If a second front end appears (CLI, web, mobile), it should consume `muninn-core` and
  `muninn-graph` directly rather than growing `muninn-ui`.
- Add a crate only when it has a clear owner and dependency direction; update `allowed_edges`
  in `xtask/src/main.rs` at the same time.

# State machines in Muninn

Implicit state is how this app currently works: a pile of `Option<T>`
and boolean fields on `State` whose *combination* decides what the user
sees and which keys do what. This document makes those machines explicit so
a change to one row can't silently change another. The refactor that
introduced it added one enum + two functions and changed no
behaviour: `pub enum Layer`, `State::topmost_layer`, `State::dismiss_layer`,
pinned by `crates/muninn-ui/tests/state_layers.rs`.

## The two axes

Overlay types and behaviour now live in `overlay.rs` (palette, Settings,
Help, layer stack) and mode transitions in `mode.rs` (`Mode`/`Scope`); the
`State` fields behind them stay in `state.rs` so the struct's invariants are
still visible in one place.

- **Page** (`Mode`): Editor, Preview, Graph. What the main column draws.
- **Overlay stack** (`Layer`): what Escape dismisses, one per press, top
  first. This section is the dismissal order.

Escape always peels the topmost layer; with no layer open, Escape in Graph
returns to the note mode. One press never closes two layers.

# Local Graph

The local graph keeps the selected note and its immediate neighbours. It answers a different
question from the global map: not *what is in the vault*, but *what is around this idea*.

Open it from the links rail, or press `⌘L` while the graph is open to switch between **Global**
and **Local**.

**Muninn** is a local-first Markdown notes app with an Obsidian-style wikilink graph, written in Rust and built on the Rune UI toolkit.

A folder of `.md` files is the whole database. Notes stay ordinary files you can read, move, diff, or put in version control. Links are written as `[[Note]]`, `[[Note|alias]]`, or `[[Note#heading]]`. The app indexes them and draws the result as a graph.

What you can do in the app:

- **Write, Read, and Graph** views of the same note, with autosave, search, a folder sidebar, and a links rail (outgoing links and backlinks).
- **Global and Local** graphs. Local shows the open note and its immediate neighbours. The layout is a force-directed graph you can pan, zoom, pin, and drive from the keyboard.
- Unresolved wikilinks stay in the text and can create the missing note when clicked. Attachments (images, PDFs) are files, not notes.
- Optional **manual sync** of one vault to one provider: GitHub, Google Drive (`drive.appdata` only), or a Tailscale tailnet. Notes remain the source of truth. Tokens stay in the OS credential store. Conflicts are kept as both copies.
- Headless checks without a window: `--check` (broken links, duplicate titles) and `--list-links`.

The workspace is split so domain logic stays testable and separate from the UI:

| Crate | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `muninn-core` | Vault, notes, wikilinks |
| `muninn-graph` | Graph layout and camera |
| `muninn-sync` | Sync planning and transfer |
| `muninn-ui` | State, rendering, input |
| `muninn-app` | Binary entry point |

There is no Muninn account and no telemetry. Preferences live in a small local settings file.
